**Verdict: PASS for DG4 round 9 (candidate `sha256:18c18fe4…`, source `f2ae717`). I raised no new findings.**

**Candidate and product**
- The candidate ID matches every time I computed it, at the start and the end: on a full clone at the freeze commit `01ad2e1`, at `f2ae717` itself, and on the repository. It covers 1475 files.
- The product code is unchanged. Between round 8's `5cd1e06` and `f2ae717`, no file outside `docs/delivery/` changed. The product files also match round 7's `dab4562`.
- One small note: that diff also contains round-8 review material, not only the records the assignment lists. All of it is under `docs/delivery/`.
- Two run-record commits from the other reviewers landed during my run, both only under `docs/delivery/runs/DG4`. The candidate ID was unchanged, and I did not read them.

**The history rewrite (D-136)**
- Comparing the backup ref with `a445b24` shows exactly the 33 restored run files, all additions, each identical to its original content.
- I checked all 360 old→new commit pairs in the map, not just three:
  - all 360 keep the same subject, author and dates;
  - none differs outside the restored files;
  - all make the same product changes.
- The project's write-once check reports 99 errors on the old history and 0 on the new one, as D-136 says.
- The other three record defects are fixed:
  - **B1:** the frozen `decisions.md` contains D-135 and D-136.
  - **B2:** all 23 closed findings are back to FIXED_PENDING_VERIFICATION with full commit ids.
  - **B4:** each round's freeze time now matches its manifest, for rounds 1–9.
- D-136 is accurate. One small note: D-135 still cites the old commit id `16e5343`, which is now `e8f14db`. The commit map resolves it, and it has no effect.

**Re-verified findings**

| Finding | Severity | Result |
|---|---|---|
| F-DG4-140 | Low | PASS → CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG4-141 | Low | PASS → CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG4-143 | Medium | PASS → CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG4-144 | Low | PASS → CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG4-145 | Low | PASS → CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG4-146 | Low | PASS → CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG4-147 | Low | PASS → CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG4-148 | Low, not mandatory | PASS → ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION |

- For each of the seven closures:
  - every fix commit is in the source's history;
  - each maps to its old id with identical product changes;
  - the fix files are unchanged in the candidate.
- I re-ran the F-DG4-146 code mutations: the tests still catch them, with the same counts as round 7.
- **F-DG4-148 (`pnpm test`):** my first series of four runs went above the load limit of 8 (peak 11.67). Part of the cause was my own git checks overlapping its start. All four of those runs passed, but they don't count. The second series stayed within the limit (peak 5.81). It ran on Node 22 and 24, with the locale unset and with `LANG=C.UTF-8`, and all four passed:
  - 1589 node unit tests;
  - 1347 web unit tests;
  - 259 more, plus 2 tests skipped by design.

**Other checks run this round**
- All 7 static checks exit 0: build, typecheck, lint, openapi:lint, no-cdn, format and contrast.
- All 5 validator commands pass, on both the repository and the clone: historical DG3, DG2 and DG1, register DG4, and pipeline.
- All 137 requirement rows are IMPLEMENTED, with no missing evidence paths, and the register is unchanged since round 7.

**Not re-run this round**
These were not re-run, because the product code is identical. My round-7 evidence is cited instead:
- the integration suite (twice);
- `tests/qa` on its own;
- the REQ-DLV-036 test counts;
- the full e2e runs in English and Arabic, under both locale settings;
- the axe, 390 px, 200 % text and auditor read-only checks.

**Expected failures shown in my logs**
- The code-mutation runs exit 1 because the tests caught the mutations.
- The write-once check exits 1 on the old history because it reproduces the defect the rewrite fixed.
- Two of my helper scripts read the wrong key, and the corrected output is appended in the same log.
- Every unit log has 14 React duplicate-key warnings from test data, the same as rounds 6–8.

**Cleanup:** I removed the disposable clone and the store copy. My first removal command was refused by a safety check because it used `$TMPDIR` in the paths. I re-ran it with the literal paths, and it worked.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG4/round-9/`:
- `qa-verifier.json`
- `qa-verifier.verifications.json`
- `qa-verifier.md`

Test evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG4/qa/round-9/`. The review record passes the schema check, and all 146 evidence references exist. No product approval (G1–G6) was given.
